Matt/Team —

Draft technical notes and attachments attached. Key points summarized below for Simon/CloudOps: 

- Topology: Primary (APAC region) —> cold-standby (EU region) is implemented as unidirectional peering where the standby has a read-only sync of model artifacts and configuration via our pull-only replication over a TLS 1.3 tunnel. No customer-produced PII or request logs are replicated.
- Egress & routing policy: All customer request payloads for EU tenants terminate in EU; any telemetry emitted by the runtime is aggregated at 1-minute intervals, hashed, and forwarded to a metrics collector in Redwood-hosted control plane (only aggregated counters, no request/response details).
- Peering controls: mTLS between VPCs, mutual certs via customer-managed CA or Redwood-managed CA (customer choice). We recommend mTLS with cert rotation every 90 days for the standby link.
- Failover behavior (cold-standby): Failover requires an explicit promotion action by CloudOps (documented in peering-runbook.md). During promotion we run the residency-validation suite (see step list below) to confirm no dangling cross-region flows.

Acceptance test checklist (short):
1) Baseline traffic capture — confirm EU tenant traffic ingress is seen only in EU ingress range (sample pcap + iptables dump).
2) Metadata audit — verify telemetry samples are hashed and aggregate-only (spot-check logs).
3) Standby pull verification — confirm artifact pulls are signed and timestamped, and payloads contain only model weights/config (no user data).
4) Idempotent promotion dry-run — simulate promotion without updating the DNS/bgp announcements and validate resident-request behavior.

Attached: network-diagram-v2.png (PNG, 310KB), peering-runbook.md (Markdown, 6KB). I'll add a small iptables snippet and a sample tcpdump command to the runbook.
